scenario: [LTIM.10.3]: a conversion between a temporal value and text resolves no zone. The ISO-8601 cast ([LCST.4.5.9]) and the `to_string` member ([LTIM.8.1.2]) write the value's own offset ([LTIM.8.2.4]) and look up no `TimeZoneOffset` fact ([LTIM.10.7]), so neither is a zone read ([LTIM.2.4.1]). A `where` holding them on a rule with two positive patterns is not time-dependent, and [LTIM.2.6.2] does not refuse it. `Arm a` and `Event e where e.k == a.k and (e.fired::String) == "2026-01-01T09:00:00Z" and e.fired.to_string("iso8601") == "2026-01-01T09:00:00Z"` compiles. `compile_ok`. PATH: `dsc.validate.ltim_2_6_2_clock_where`'s `time_read`, whose zone arm, `dsc.typecheck.ltim_2_4_1_zone_read`, matches `local` and `date` alone.
rules_ds:
use default

schema Arm scope logical:
    k: Int key

schema Event scope logical:
    k: Int key
    fired: Time mutable

rule at_nine:
    Arm a
    Event e where e.k == a.k and (e.fired::String) == "2026-01-01T09:00:00Z" and e.fired.to_string("iso8601") == "2026-01-01T09:00:00Z"
->
    log info "at nine"
